Subject: Eval acceptance — surface risk thresholds and mitigation plan

Team, Alex — quick heads up from the eval run on promptset_v4 we shipped to the AB cohort yesterday. We’re seeing a small but consistent degradation for the L2 factuality metric (~2.4% relative) on long-form prompts (>= 400 tokens). I want to get alignment on whether that delta is acceptable under our current acceptance rules and, if not, a concrete remediation/rollback plan we can execute with minimal customer impact.

Quick context:
- Model variant: rwd-infer-3b-q4 (quantized)
- A/B cohort: AtlasAI production traffic (via DEAL-4317) — 10% traffic, run for 24h
- Observed: factuality drop concentrated on long prompts; latency and token cost unchanged
- Relevant artifacts: promptset_v4.csv (attached), AB plan notes (attached), run logs on Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

Options I want us to discuss:
1) Declare a soft failure and pause rollout while we investigate (fast rollback to rwd-infer-3b-fp16)
2) Keep canary but tighten acceptance criteria for long-form slices (raise sample size + require zero degradation on factuality)
3) Deploy targeted mitigation (prefix caching tweaks + prompt normalization) and observe for 12 hours

My recommendation: short pause + deeper triage to confirm signal and root cause. If this is a quantization regression we should prefer rollback for Atlas (enterprise SLA). For self-serve customers we could try 3) as a lower-risk test.

Asks:
- Marissa: can you confirm whether this crosses the existing eval acceptance threshold for DEAL-4317 and whether the contract requires immediate rollback?
- Karthik: what’s the fastest safe path to rollback to the fp16 variant (time to spin new pool, routing changes, and any infra gotchas)?
- Evelyn: can you triage the dataset slice and provide a minimal repro prompt list so we can send to model-ops?
- Alex / Rachel: how do you want us to proceed from Atlas’ side — immediate rollback or let us run a short mitigation?

Thanks — Vivek
